Details
  • Paper: StableNormal: Reducing Diffusion Variance for Stable and Sharp Normal, SIGGRAPH Asia 2024, 2024-06-24
  • Original code: https://github.com/Stable-X/StableNormal at 594b934630ab
  • Code licence: Apache-2.0 (permissive); files: LICENSE
  • Weights licence: Apache-2.0
  • Licence evidence: https://github.com/Stable-X/StableNormal/blob/594b934630ab3bc71f35c77d14ec7feb98480cd0/LICENSE.txt (Apache-2.0); https://huggingface.co/Stable-X/yoso-normal-v0-3/blob/2202fcb69960d94b437e06c19c556a12ceeb57c0/README.md (license: apache-2.0)
  • Training data: Stable Diffusion 2 (LAION-5B subsets) fine-tuned on synthetic and real normals datasets (Hypersim, Replica, ScanNet and others per the StableNormal paper, arXiv 2406.16864)
  • Options: long_side = 768 (>= 0; also processing_res), seed = 0
  • Kernel libraries: cudnn_hacc
  • Variants: stablenormal-turbo
  • Outputs: normals; kind: none
  • Input size: any H x W >= 1, resized or padded inside the model
  • Tested up to (portable, fp16, RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB): stablenormal-turbo 3000x4000 (3.6 GiB peak allocated, 4.8 reserved)
  • stablenormal-turbo 994x1482, first call: portable + torch.compile 76 s (cold Inductor cache).
  • stablenormal-turbo original 994x1482: the authors' mixed-precision option (float16); upstream YOSONormalsPipeline (turbo, t_start 0), diffusers 0.41.0, latents seed 0
  • stablenormal-turbo load / first call: original 6.36 s / 1.128 s, portable 2.94 s / 0.544 s, kernels 3.25 s / 0.352 s
  • Protocol, first call, 3 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3 rounds x median of 5

Measured

AbsRel / delta1 after a least-squares scale + shift fit (in disparity space for inverse-depth models), mean over images. Original = the original code named under Details, same checkpoint and protocol.

Parity

CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 1e-05 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.00046 and p99 <= 0.0021 (absolute error of the output normals).

Limitations

  • Normals only: no depth.
  • Diffusion model: the seeded noise comes from a CPU generator; upstream draws it from the unseeded global RNG, so its outputs vary from call to call (slightly).
  • Upstream's Predictor wrapper (pre-resize to a multiple of 64 near 1024 px, uint8 round trip, LANCZOS back) is not applied: the runners follow its pipeline (768 px).
  • A traced or exported module reuses the noise of its traced shape.
